chunks: Ibn Faḍḍāl, from ʿAbdullāh ibn al-Mughīrah, who said:

I was Waqifī, and I performed hajj in that state. Then when I came to Makkah, something stirred in my chest, so I clung to al-Multazam. Then I said: O Allah, You have indeed known my seeking and my intention, so guide me to the best of religions. Then it occurred within me that I should go to al-Riḍā عليه السلام.

So I came to al-Madīnah and stood at his door, and I said to the servant: Tell your master that a man from the people of Iraq is at the door. He said: Then I heard his call while he was saying: Enter, O ʿAbdullāh ibn al-Mughīrah, enter, O ʿAbdullāh ibn al-Mughīrah. So I entered, and when he looked at me, he said to me: Allah has answered your supplication and guided you to His religion. So I said: I bear witness that you are the hujjah of Allah and His trustee over His creation.

key_terms.أَمِينُهُ: His trustee; one entrusted by Allah over creation
key_terms.إِرَادَتِي: my intention; his inward aim and resolve
key_terms.الْمُلْتَزَمِ: the place at the Kaʿbah where he clung in supplication
key_terms.حُجَّةُ اللَّهِ: the divine proof of Allah; a title affirming the Imam’s authority
key_terms.دُعَاءَكَ: your supplication; the prayer Allah answered
key_terms.دِينِهِ: His religion; the true religion to which he was guided
key_terms.طَلِبَتِي: my seeking; the spiritual quest he presented before Allah

ai.seo_question: How did ʿAbdullāh ibn al-Mughīrah come to recognize Imam al-Riḍā عليه السلام as the hujjah of Allah?
ai.summary: This narration recounts how ʿAbdullāh ibn al-Mughīrah, while previously holding Waqifī beliefs, sought guidance from Allah at al-Multazam during hajj. He was inwardly directed to Imam al-Riḍā عليه السلام, whose immediate recognition of him and response to his supplication led him to testify to the Imam’s divine authority.

en.hubeali: Ibn Fazzal, from Abdullah Bin Al Mugheira who said,

‘I was Waqifiite and I performed Hajj being upon that state. So when I came to Makkah, something disturbed me in my chest, so I attached with Al-Multazim (a wall of the Kaaba), then I said, ‘O Allah<sup>azwj</sup>! You<sup>azwj</sup> have Known of my seeking and my intention, therefore Guide me to the best of the Religions’. So there occurred within myself that I should go to Al-Reza<sup>asws</sup>.

So I went over to Al-Medina and paused at his<sup>asws</sup> door and said to the slave, ‘Tell your Master<sup>asws</sup> that a man from the people of Al-Iraq is at the door’. So I heard his<sup>asws</sup> call and he<sup>asws</sup> was saying: ‘Enter, O Abdullah Bin Al-Mugheira! Enter, O Abdullah Bin Al Mugheira!’ So I entered. So when he<sup>asws</sup> looked at me, he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Allah<sup>azwj</sup> has Answered your supplication and Guided you to His<sup>azwj</sup> Religion’. So I said, ‘I testify that you<sup>asws</sup> are the Divine Authority of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> and His<sup>azwj</sup> Trustee upon His<sup>azwj</sup> creatures’.
en.sarwar: 13. Ibn Faddall has narrated from ‘Abdallah ibn al-Mughira who has said the following.

“I was a member of Waqifa sect and I wen to Hajj with the same belief. When I arrived in Makka an idea began to prick my chest. I got hold of al-Multazam (the wall next to the door of Ka‘ba) and said, “O Lord, You know what I ask for and my intention. Guide me to the best of the religions. It then occurred to me to see al-Rida (a.s.).

I went to the city of Madina and stood in front of his door and said to his slave, ‘Tell your master that a man from Iraq is at the door.’” He has said that I heard his voice saying, “O ‘Abdallah ibn Mughira, come in.” I then went inside and when he looked at me he said, “Allah has answered your prayer and has guided you to His religion.” I then said, “I testify that you possess Divine Authority and you are the trustee of Allah over His creatures.” :
